# Submission acceptance fixture

This is a synthetic equipment-borrowing module for disposable applications, using native application authentication. It adds an asset tag, `CUSTOM-` validation, a business permission gate, custom blue border, and a lifecycle approval transition whose transaction inserts an inventory entry. Never install these test-only routes into an application with real data; the permission switch exists only to exercise revocation. The real equipment-borrowing application is not required or accessed.

## Fresh application

Create the application with `pnpm create @nocobase/app submission-new --template=<target-template-directory-or-package> --no-install --json`, from a scratch working directory. Verify its `nocobase.templatePackage`, read its `AGENTS.md` and synchronized application Skills, and install the target's coordinated dependencies. For an unreleased source-workspace verification, link the generated application's `node_modules` to the target template's installed workspace modules; this exercises the pending source and is not a published-version certification. Do not run package-manager mutations through that shared link.

Copy `migration.ts` to `database/main/migrations/202610260099_submission_fixture.ts`, `routes.ts` to `server/routes/submission-fixture.ts`, and `page.tsx` to `client/pages/submission-fixture.tsx`. Register the server contribution in `server/routes/index.ts`, preserving the template's submission provider. Add an authenticated application route at `/submission-check`, with `authz: 'skip'` and a component loader for the fixture page. The fixture's business endpoints own their authentication and synthetic permission gate independently of that page setting.

Run `pnpm nocobase config init --dialect sqlite --json`, then start with `APP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:<chosen-port> APP_SERVER_PORT=<chosen-port> I18N_DEFAULT_LOCALE=en-US pnpm dev`. Use the actual printed application entry URL, including its base path. Configuration initialization generates local secrets; do not publish its file or native session cookies.

## Customized source upgrade

Prepare a separate application from the BASE template, before this feature. Add the same custom business schema, validation, permission gate, style and lifecycle hook. For the pre-upgrade page, replace only the shared controller with a direct submit function and omit operation headers on Repository mutations. For its custom action call `runtime.fire` without the new outer receipt adapter. Start it on its own database, sign in through its own native login and reproduce two records from a double click while holding the first response. Preserve these synthetic record ids and complete JSON rows as the data baseline.

Stop the old application and commit its source baseline on a local branch. Back up its closed database and migration history. Reconcile BASE → TARGET and BASE → PROJECT through the [submission source-upgrade checklist](../../../../../app/app-skills/skills/nocobase-app-upgrade/references/submission-upgrade.md). Merge the provider/registration, receipt migration, three settings forms and client peer dependencies. For the customized page change only the controller and key forwarding; preserve the fields, validation and styling. For its custom server action add the receipt adapter around the existing lifecycle transition and join its transaction, preserving the permission check and inventory hook. Keep all business tables and records. Inspect `db apply --dry-run` and `db repair --dry-run`; this additive feature should add only the receipt migration with no old checksum changes. Apply it, restart the same application and retain its original database.

For an unreleased source target, report its commit and keep the existing release marker instead of inventing a published target version. For a published target, advance `defaultTemplateVersion` only after source reconciliation and validation. Restore the paired old source and database backup for recovery.

## Run the browser matrix

Set `SUBMISSION_APPLICATIONS` to a JSON array of `{ "name": "new-template", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/main" }` and `{ "name": "upgraded-customized", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<other-port>/main", "beforeData": "<path-to-pre-upgrade-evidence-JSON>" }`. `beforeData` contains the fixture's `{ rows, entries, history }`, captured from its authenticated evidence endpoint before upgrading. Write the environment setup to a local file when it spans multiple lines. Use the synthetic initial administrator from the disposable template; never reuse a management-instance identity or credential.

Run the application's local `pnpm exec playwright test -c tests/fixtures/submission/playwright.config.ts`. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` must name an allowed scratch directory when installing a browser; use that same directory to run it. `SUBMISSION_EVIDENCE_DIR` selects a scratch output directory. The dedicated configuration keeps this opt-in fixture out of ordinary template browser tests. The test neither sleeps nor automatically retries failures.

Each application checks validation and custom styling, double click, Enter plus programmatic submit while a committed response is held, normal identical new records, update, a definite server rejection with retained input, response loss after a server-confirmed commit, unchanged keys and bodies on retry, refusal of changed input during an uncertain operation, permission revocation, and lifecycle approval with exactly one history entry and inventory effect. Every original row must remain identical. English submitting/error/success screenshots and JSON invariant summaries are attached to the Playwright result. The service-level suites separately cover parallel HTTP attempts, rollback, changed-content conflicts, expiration after cleanup, strict/compatibility modes and query costs on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL.
